previous_disclosures.section: Regulatory and Other Matters > Other Matters
previous_disclosures.summary: Goldman Sachs narrowed its focus on consumer-related activities in 2023 and 2024 by completing the sale of the Marcus loan portfolio, its PFM business, and the majority of the GreenSky loan portfolio, as well as selling its seller financing loan portfolio. In 2024, the company also agreed to transition the GM credit card program to another issuer, expected to complete in Q3 2025, while committing to support products and customers during these transitions.

Equity positions primarily relate to investments in corporate, real estate, and infrastructure assets within Asset & Wealth Management, while debt positions include mezzanine/senior debt, corporate/real estate loans in Asset & Wealth Management, and specific held-for-sale credit card and GreenSky loans in Platform Solutions.
A table presenting Platform Solutions assets is referenced in the filing.

peer_results.rationale: The retrieved candidates for BAC focus on aggregate commercial real estate loan balances (D053) and overall net charge-off drivers including credit cards and small business loans (D320). While BAC discloses CRE exposure, it does not isolate a specific Wealth Management segment exposure comparable to GS's Asset & Wealth Management breakdown, nor does it provide specific charge-off amounts for a Wealth Management CRE portfolio distinct from its general consumer/commercial pools in the supplied text.

The retrieved candidates for Citi focus on total consolidated credit exposure to commercial real estate (D193) and aggregate Wealth segment loan/deposit balances (D116). Citi's CRE exposure disclosure is consolidated across corporate and wealth clients without isolating a specific Wealth Management loan portfolio comparable to GS's Asset & Wealth Management specific debt positions. The Wealth segment disclosure lists loan categories but does not detail CRE composition or risks specific to that segment's holdings in the same manner as GS.

The retrieved candidates for JPM focus on residential real estate portfolios (D346) and Home Lending loans held-for-sale (D116). GS's disclosure concerns corporate/real estate debt and private equity investments within Asset & Wealth Management. JPM's residential real estate focus (prime mortgages and HELOCs) is a different asset class and segment (Consumer/Home Lending) than GS's commercial/corporate wealth management holdings, making them not sufficiently comparable on the specific topic of Asset & Wealth Management debt/equity composition.

comparisons.peer_summary: During 2024, the firm incurred $25 million in charge-offs for Wealth Management commercial real estate loans, primarily within the office sector.
comparisons.comparison: Both Goldman Sachs (GS) and Morgan Stanley (MS) disclose specific exposures to commercial real estate (CRE) within their Wealth Management divisions, but GS reports the composition of its positions for sensitivity analysis while MS reports actual credit losses (charge-offs). GS discloses that debt positions in Asset & Wealth Management include corporate and real estate loans. MS discloses that it incurred $25 million in charge-offs for Wealth Management commercial real estate loans in 2024, primarily in the office sector, indicating realized credit deterioration in that specific asset class, whereas GS's disclosure focuses on the potential market risk (10% decline in value) of such positions without citing specific charge-off amounts for the period.

sentences.text: • Debt positions include mezzanine and senior debt, and corporate and real estate loans, substantially all of which are included within Asset & Wealth Management. Debt positions also included approximately $1.8 billion as of December 2024 and approximately $2.0 billion as of December 2023 of GM co-branded credit card loans, and approximately $3.0 billion as of December 2023 of GreenSky loans that were classified as held for sale. These held for sale loans were included within Platform Solutions.
During 2024, there were charge-offs of Wealth Management commercial real estate loans of $25 million, mainly in the office sector.
